Article Title: ‘Deeply shameful’: Tharoor slams UK over colonialism omission in slavery apology
Article Text:
Shashi Tharoor slams UK PM over proposed slavery apology, questions omission of colonialism. (File photo)​

The Guardian

Tharoor says colonialism cannot be left out

Tharoor's remarks followed Burnham's remark over Britain's involvement in the slave trade.

Burnham pitches for 'honest conversation' on slavery

Inglorious Empire: What the British Did to India

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor has criticised British prime minister Andy Burnham for considering an apology for Britain's role in the trans-Atlantic slave trade while leaving out its colonial past.The Thiruvananthapuram Lok Sabha MP described the omission as “inexplicable and inexcusable”, arguing that Britain must also acknowledge the suffering caused by its colonial rule.Tharoor's remarks followed Burnham's announcement that his government would consider issuing a formal apology for Britain's involvement in the slave trade as part of efforts to strengthen ties with countries in Africa and the Caribbean.In an article published inon Saturday, Burnham said Britain needed to confront its “complicated history” to protect the future of the Commonwealth, a grouping of 56 independent countries that largely emerged from the former British Empire.Burnham is scheduled to visit Antigua and Barbuda this week for a meeting of Commonwealth leaders.Responding to Burnham's remarks in a post on X on Saturday, Tharoor said he had long maintained that putting a monetary figure on the damage caused by British rule was difficult."But moral atonement for the ravages of colonialism is indispensable. I am glad to learn that Prime Minister Burnham is prepared to offer a formal apology on behalf of the British state for the horrors of slavery. But the omission of colonialism from his apology is inexplicable and inexcusable," the MP from Thiruvananthapuram said.He also said Britain had never formally apologised for the destruction and exploitation carried out during its colonial rule."It remains deeply shameful that Britain has never said a simple 'sorry' for the loot, pillage, death and destruction perpetrated during the colonial era on millions of innocent victims of British imperialism," he said.In his article, Burnham said countries affected by the trans-Atlantic slave trade had repeatedly sought an acknowledgement of its lasting consequences.“For years, those members of the Commonwealth affected by the slave trade have asked for an honest conversation about the legacies of slavery,” Burnham was quoted as saying by media reports. “By sticking our heads in the sand, we have damaged the ability of the Commonwealth to function.”Tharoor, who has written extensively about British colonial rule, is the author of. The book examines how British rule led to the systematic exploitation and plunder of India's wealth.
Article Summary: Shashi Tharoor slams UK PM over proposed slavery apology, questions omission of colonialism. UK PM Andy Burnham said his government would consider issuing a formal apology for Britain's involvement in the slave trade as part of efforts to strengthen ties with countries in Africa and the Caribbean.

Article Title: DGCA mandates twin pilot operations from Monday, chopper operators threaten to suspend Char Dam flights
Article Text:
Chopper operators on Char Dham routes have threatened to suspend operations from Monday over DGCA's mandatory twin-pilot rule, citing unviable costs, after a crash killed six people.

NEW DELHI: Chopper operations on Char Dham routes could come to standstill from Monday. Following a chopper crashing soon after take off from Badrinath on Friday (October 30), killing all six people on board — a pilot and five passengers, the DGCA has made it mandatory for choppers operating on Char Dham to be manned by two pilots starting Monday (Nov 2), in a bid to improve safety. However chopper operators have termed the move unviable and threatened to suspend these sorties from Monday “until the matter is reviewed and a mutually workable solution is arrived at.Chopper operators on Saturday sent their “collective objection to the implementation of mandatory twin-pilot operations and intimation of suspension of operations from Nov 2, 2026,” to Directorate General of Civil Aviation chief Vir Vikram Yadav. “… (we) collectively place on record our serious concern and reservation regarding the mandatory requirement of twin-pilot operations for charter services (in) the new operational restrictions communicated by DGCA proposed to be implemented with effect from the first take-off on Nov 2, 2026. ”“The mandatory deployment of two pilots on every charter sortie will substantially increase operating costs, crew requirements, accommodation and logistical expenses, and overall operational commitments.Given the existing commercial structure, prevailing charter rates and limited operational margins, these additional costs cannot be reasonably absorbed by the operators. Nor is it commercially feasible to pass on the entire additional burden to customers,” it says.“… all operators have consistently complied with applicable DGCA regulations and have invested considerable resources in maintaining safe, efficient and reliable operations in the challenging Himalayan terrain…. any additional safety-related measures must be practical, proportionate, commercially sustainable and developed in consultation with the operating stakeholders. Accordingly, after due consideration and mutual consultation, all operators collectively express their inability to accept the mandatory twin-pilot requirement in its present form,” it says."In view of the above, we wish to formally convey that all participating operators are proposing to suspend their Char Dham charter operations with effect from Nov 2, 2026, until the matter is reviewed and a mutually workable solution is arrived at by the concerned authorities in consultation with the operators. Under the proposed framework, continuing operations would result in unsustainable financial and operational commitments, leaving the operators with no commercially viable alternative,” it said.Operators have DGCA and Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority (UCADA) to "reconsider the mandatory twin-pilot requirement, engage with all stakeholders on an urgent basis, and explore an alternative operational framework that adequately addresses safety concerns while ensuring the commercial viability and sustainability of helicopter operations in the region. We remain committed to aviation safety, regulatory compliance and the continued development of helicopter services in Uttarakhand. We hope that the matter will receive urgent consideration and that a constructive resolution can be reached before the proposed implementation date.”
Article Summary: Chopper operators on Char Dham routes have threatened to suspend operations from Monday over DGCA's mandatory twin-pilot rule. They cite unviable costs, after a crash killed six people. Following a chopper crashing soon after take off from Badrinath on Friday (October 30), killing all six people on board — a pilot and five passengers.

Article Title: 'Why do you challenge democracy?' BJP chief Nitin Nabin accuses Rahul Gandhi of acting on behest of foreign powers
Article Text:
Nitin Nabin accuses Rahul Gandhi of relying on ‘3 crore infiltrators’ instead of voters

Nabin challenges opposition on voter deletion claims

BJP leader raises 1984 anti-Sikh riots , targets Gandhi family

NEW DELHI: BJP national president Nitin Nabin on Sunday accused Congress leader Rahul Gandhi of acting at the behest of foreign powers, alleging that the opposition was attempting to create instability and challenge an elected government under the pretext of defending democracy.Addressing the BJP's 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' (Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy) march in Haryana ’s Rohtak, Nabin said the party's campaign was aimed at countering what he described as a deliberate attempt to spread chaos across the country.Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD) president Jayant Chaudhary was also present on the stage.“As we participate in this 'Save Democracy' march, we must address the atmosphere of chaos and instability that is being deliberately spread throughout the nation,” Nabin said.He alleged that Rahul Gandhi was working to further the agendas of foreign powers and seeking to challenge India's democratic system at their direction.“They are the same purveyors of chaos who have recently been sowing discord abroad. Their associates, members of the Communist Party and certain Congress leaders, talk about 'changing the regime.' But this is a government formed by the mandate of the people; no one can even lay a finger on it,” he said.Nabin also questioned the Congress's criticism of electoral outcomes, arguing that the party accepted democratic mandates when it won elections but raised concerns over the electoral process when it lost.“You (Congress) have no faith in the country’s 1.4 billion people. In whom, then, do you place your trust? In 3 crore infiltrators! I ask you, Rahul Gandhi: what exactly is your intention? Why do you challenge democracy?” he said.Citing electoral outcomes in different states, Nabin said the Congress described democracy as having prevailed when it won in Himachal Pradesh and Karnataka, but claimed it was under threat after losing in Haryana, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal.He further accused the Congress of seeking to run the country according to the wishes of the Gandhi family, saying that governance should instead be guided by the Constitution.BJP president also targeted the Congress over its allegations of irregularities in electoral rolls and criticism of the Election Commission of India (ECI).Referring to the 1975 Allahabad High Court judgment that set aside then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi's election from Rae Bareli, Nabin accused the Congress of having a history of misusing government machinery during elections.“When Indira Gandhi won an election, the Allahabad High Court ruled that she had won by misusing the entire govt machinery and employing improper means. Her election was completely annulled, and she was barred from contesting elections for six years,” he said.He also challenged Rahul Gandhi's claims regarding the deletion of 13 crore votes, saying the BJP and its National Democratic Alliance (NDA) partners were prepared to provide details of the deletions.“Today, they claim that 13 crore votes have been deleted. I say to you, Rahul Gandhi, that any worker from our party, the NDA, or even one of our local unit presidents can provide a detailed account for every single one of those 13 crore deleted votes,” Nabin said.He added that the BJP was willing to discuss the issue either in public or in Parliament. Nabin also accused the Congress of seeking to protect infiltrators and said BJP and NDA workers would work to ensure their removal from the country.Nabin also criticised the Congress over the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, arguing that the party should have apologised for the violence instead of taking part in protests on the issue of electoral integrity.He referred to former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi's remark after the assassination of Indira Gandhi that “when a big tree falls, the earth shakes”, saying it should have prompted remorse from the Congress leadership.“When our Sikh brethren were being slaughtered, when a full-scale massacre was unfolding, your father remarked that 'when a big tree falls, the earth shakes.' Because of that 'shaking of the earth,' the lives of so many of my Sikh brothers were extinguished. You should have felt remorse for this; you should have apologised,” he said.The BJP president also accused the Congress of practising dynastic politics and alleged that its leaders followed the directions of the Gandhi family rather than democratic principles.His remarks came as the INDIA bloc held its 'Chalo Dilli' march from the Minto Road-Connaught Place junction to Ramlila Maidan in Delhi on Sunday.The opposition alliance is protesting against alleged irregularities in electoral rolls during the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise and has demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi had alleged that shops in Connaught Place were forcibly shut ahead of the march, causing losses to local traders. In a post on X, he said the opposition had encouraged rally participants to shop in the area but found commercial establishments closed.The BJP also organised a separate march in West Delhi to remember the victims of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, accusing the Congress of holding its political rally on the anniversary of the violence.
Article Summary: BJP leader Nitin Nabin accuses Rahul Gandhi of relying on ‘3 crore infiltrators’ instead of voters. Nabin challenges opposition on voter deletion claims. BJP leader raises 1984 anti-Sikh riots, targets Gandhi family.

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Sunday accused the Bharatiya Janata Party ( BJP ) of causing financial losses to local traders by allegedly forcing shops in Delhi's Connaught Place to shut on the day of the INDIA bloc's 'Chalo Delhi' march and mega rally at Ramlila Maidan. The Leader of the Opposition claimed that the closures hurt businesses despite his appeal to rally participants to support local traders by shopping in the capital.In a post on X on Sunday, Rahul said participants travelling to the national capital had been encouraged to shop at local markets during their visit. However, he claimed that they found shops closed upon reaching Connaught Place."We told everyone that when you come here for the march and the mega rally, buy things, do some shopping. But, while coming to Connaught Place here, we found out that the BJP has forcibly shut down every single shop. So, you should know who is causing the loss to the traders, and how it's happening!" Rahul said.The remarks followed an appeal Rahul had made in a video message on X late on Saturday, urging people arriving in Delhi from different parts of the country to support small businesses during the festive season."Tomorrow, lakhs of people are coming to Delhi for the Ramlila March.It is the festive season. The time of Diwali, Chhath, and Bhai Dooj has arrived. I want those lakhs of people coming to Delhi from outside to support the traders here," he said."Protest, march, hold rallies, and along with that, do a little shopping too - it will benefit the traders," Rahul added.The Congress leader also rejected concerns that the gathering would hurt businesses, accusing the BJP of spreading rumours about the rally's economic impact."I know the rally will not harm the traders. The BJP is scared, that's why it's spreading rumours," he said, reiterating his appeal for participants to purchase goods from local shops.The appeal came amid objections from traders' associations, which had urged Rahul and Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi to postpone the November 1 demonstration until after the festive season.The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) warned that an estimated 10 lakh participants and 15,000-20,000 vehicles could cause severe congestion across central Delhi."We demand to reschedule the mega-rally of 1 million (10 lakh) people, planned for November 1, to a date after Diwali; lack of parking for 15,000–20,000 vehicles could lead to a total gridlock, akin to a lockdown," the traders' body said.The Federation of Sadar Bazar Traders Association also flagged the potential impact on festive business, estimating that the period from Dhanteras to Diwali accounts for around Rs 25,000 crore in turnover. It sought postponement of the rally until after November 10.Meanwhile, thousands of supporters and senior opposition leaders gathered in the national capital on Sunday for the INDIA bloc's 'Chalo Delhi' protest march and mega rally at Ramlila Maidan, prompting heightened security arrangements and traffic restrictions across parts of central Delhi.Several prominent leaders, including Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Priyanka Gandhi, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, AICC General Secretary KC Venugopal, West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee, Trinamool Congress General Secretary Abhishek Banerjee, Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren, Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy and RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav, joined the procession after departing from the Constitution Club.Carrying banners reading 'Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao', the opposition leaders are protesting alleged electoral roll irregularities and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise. The INDIA bloc has also demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged large-scale voter omissions.
Article Summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi accuses BJP of forcing Connaught Place shops to shut. He says traders made to suffer losses despite his appeal to rally participants to support local traders by shopping in the capital. Thousands of supporters and senior opposition leaders gathered in the national capital on Sunday for the 'Chalo Delhi' protest march and mega rally.

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Sunday accused the Election Commission of depriving voters of their constitutional rights, alleging that the removal of 130 million names from electoral rolls was unacceptable.Tharoor said the campaign's message is “Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao” as several INDIA bloc leaders, including Rahul Gandhi , Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Mamata Banerjee, Farooq Abdullah, Tejashwi Yadav, Akhilesh Yadav, Supriya Sule, Abhishek Banerjee and KC Venugopal, move towards Ramlila Maidan for the mega rally.He also questioned the alleged large-scale deletion of voters' names, citing Rahul Gandhi's claim that 130 million voters had been removed.“You cannot cut 130 million voters, as Rahul Gandhi pointed out yesterday. 15 % of the Indian adult population has been cut. Article Title: 'PM Modi, Amit Shah suffering loss': Sanjay Raut on business concerns of traders ahead of INDIA bloc rally
Article Text:

INDIA bloc expects large turnout at Ramlila Maidan

NEW DELHI: Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut on Sunday dismissed concerns that the INDIA bloc's rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan would disrupt business in the national capital, taking a swipe at Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah by calling them the country's “only two traders”.Speaking to news agency ANI ahead of the opposition alliance's 'Chalo Delhi' mobilisation, Raut said any losses suffered by the two leaders as a result of the demonstration would be acceptable.He also claimed that lakhs of people were travelling to Delhi to demand a change of government and defend constitutional democracy.“There are no real concerns among the traders; in this country, the only two 'traders' are Modi ji and Shah ji. They are certainly suffering losses. If such movements cause them losses, then so be it,” Raut said.He described the mobilisation as a show of national strength rather than an event organised by any one political party, claiming that attempts to prevent people from reaching the capital would only increase the size of the gathering.“Lakhs of people are arriving. There are significant attempts to stop them, but the more they try to block people, the larger the crowd will grow.People will break through all the barricades to get here. They want a regime change. They do not want this govt,” he said.Raut added that such programmes would continue to be held in Delhi in front of the Prime Minister and the home minister.The Shiv Sena (UBT) leader also accused the Election Commission of India (ECI) of functioning under pressure from the ruling establishment, alleging that constitutional institutions had failed to maintain their independence.“Constitutional watchdogs have surrendered their autonomy. When votes are manipulated, and institutions turn a blind eye, the people of the country have no option but to demand accountability out in the open. We will not allow the Election Commission to become a front organisation for the ruling party,” he said.Raut maintained that the INDIA bloc remained united in its opposition to alleged voter roll tampering and what it described as the suppression of democratic norms.“This massive mobilisation is a loud and clear message to the government: you cannot govern this country through fear, misuse of agencies, and electoral manipulation. The voice of the people will triumph,” he added.Backing the rally, Samajwadi Party leader S T Hasan told ANI that the demonstration could become “historic” if the government allowed it to proceed without interference. The former MP said the mobilisation was aimed at protecting the Constitution and democratic values.“If the government doesn’t interfere and allows the rally to take place, it is set to be a historic one. This rally is about saving the nation, protecting the Constitution, and safeguarding our democracy,” Hasan said.He also expressed concern over what he described as a decline in the global perception of India's electoral integrity, claiming that the country was increasingly being viewed as a “pseudo-democracy”.“The message currently circulating globally is that the world’s largest democracy has effectively become a 'pseudo-democracy', a place where votes are stolen, fair elections do not occur, and the principle of 'might is right' prevails,” he said.Hasan urged citizens to support the opposition's initiative, saying it was the duty of every Indian to stand up for the country and protect democracy.The remarks came as supporters of INDIA bloc parties began gathering at Ramlila Maidan and other locations in Delhi on Sunday morning for the 'Chalo Delhi' rally against alleged electoral irregularities.The opposition alliance is also demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Congress supporters assembled outside Himachal Bhawan, while Samajwadi Party workers gathered near party chief Akhilesh Yadav's residence before proceeding towards the rally venue.Party workers from several states had also reached the capital on Saturday or earlier.The march is scheduled to begin at noon from the Minto Road-Connaught Place junction and culminate at Ramlila Maidan.Senior opposition leaders, including Rahul Gandhi , Mallikarjun Kharge, Mamata Banerjee, Abhishek Banerjee, Hemant Soren, Revanth Reddy, Tejashwi Yadav and Akhilesh Yadav, are expected to attend.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi had urged people travelling to Delhi for the protest to also shop from local traders ahead of Diwali, Chhath and Bhai Dooj. In a video message posted on X on Saturday, he said the opposition's programme would not hurt businesses and asked supporters to combine their participation in the rally with some shopping.The INDIA bloc has estimated that up to 10 lakh people could attend the mobilisation, while Delhi Police expects a turnout of around 50,000. Ramlila Maidan can accommodate 45,000 to 50,000 people when empty, but the estimated capacity is lower — around 30,000 to 40,000 — with chairs, enclosures and passageways in place.More than 4,000 police personnel, along with Central Armed Police Forces companies, are being deployed for security and crowd management. The ground has been divided into 14 zones, with each supervised by an assistant commissioner-rank officer. More than 200 CCTV cameras, drones and body-worn cameras will also be used for surveillance.The Delhi Traffic Police has announced restrictions and diversions in parts of central Delhi from 10 am to 5 pm on Sunday and advised commuters to plan their journeys accordingly, ANI reported.The mobilisation follows a symbolic 'public impeachment' of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Kharge's residence on Saturday. Former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar presided over the proceedings, during which Kharge moved a resolution listing the Opposition's charges against the CEC.Rahul Gandhi delivered the concluding remarks before the resolution was adopted.The INDIA bloc has been protesting against what it calls 'vote chori', alleging large-scale deletion of voters' names during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
Article Summary: Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut calls Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah the country's "only two traders" Raut says any losses suffered by the two leaders as a result of the demonstration would be acceptable. Samajwadi Party leader S T Hasan says the demonstration could become 'historic' if the government allows it to proceed without interference.

Article Title: 'Politicisation of energy flows harmful': Jaishankar calls for diversified supply chains at G20
Article Text:
Jaishankar speaks at the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta, calling for diversified supply chains and the de-politicisation of energy markets

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Saturday called for reducing political interference in energy markets and diversifying global supply chains, saying disruptions were placing a disproportionate burden on developing countries.Speaking about the message he delivered at G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta, Jaishankar said the discussions covered geopolitical conflicts, energy and food security, and resilient supply chains.“Look, there are big conflicts today, two major conflicts which are having global ramifications,” ANI quoted him as saying. He added that “there are no military solutions; we have to find a diplomatic pathway.”On energy security, Jaishankar warned against disruptions in fuel distribution and their impact on developing economies. “This distortion of the energy markets, the politicisation of energy flows, this is something which is very harmful,” he said, adding that “the Global South was bearing the brunt of the energy shortages and that something needs to be done.”He also flagged risks to food security, citing disruptions to grain shipments through the Black Sea and fertiliser shortages linked to tensions in the Persian Gulf and Red Sea regions.At the meeting's concluding session on supply chains, Jaishankar called for wider diversification of manufacturing and production across countries. “Today we need more diversified supply chains,” he said, advocating “more globalised, you know, more diversified production, more diversified manufacturing.”In a post on X after the session, he said securing supply chains was central to the global economy's well-being and called on the G20 to promote “the right to industrialise” and resist “predatory practices”.“Diversification and de-risking, including in connectivity, is the key to supply chain resilience, threatened by pandemics, conflicts, climate events and mishaps,” he said.Jaishankar also urged the grouping to work towards the “de-politicisation of markets” and prevent the concentration of production and resources in a few geographies.US secretary of state Marco Rubio, who hosted the meeting, also stressed the need to secure critical trade routes, including the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab el-Mandeb, and strengthen supply chains for critical minerals.On the sidelines, Jaishankar attended a Quad foreign ministers' meeting with Rubio and his Japanese and Australian counterparts. He also met Russian foreign minister Sergey Lavrov, with discussions covering the Ukraine conflict, the Gulf situation and multilateral issues.
Article Summary: S Jaishankar spoke at the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta. He called for the de-politicisation of energy markets and diversified supply chains. He said the Global South was bearing the brunt of energy shortages. He also flagged risks to food security, citing disruptions to grain shipments.

Article Title: 10 lakh turnout target, 4,000 cops, 200 CCTV: Delhi braces for INDIA bloc's anti-CEC rally at Ramlila Maidan
Article Text:
Preparations underway at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan for the INDIA bloc's anti-CEC rally

'Chalo Dilli' march to precede rally

4,000 cops, 200 CCTV cameras for security

Traffic curbs across key Delhi roads

Rally follows symbolic 'public impeachment' of CEC

NEW DELHI: Delhi is gearing up for INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan on Sunday, with opposition parties expecting a turnout of up to 10 lakh people and police deploying more than 4,000 personnel to manage security and crowds.The rally is being organised to protest against alleged electoral irregularities and demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.The mobilisation comes amid the Opposition's allegations of 'vote chori' and large-scale voter deletions during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The programme will begin with a march, called 'Chalo Dilli', from the Minto Road-Connaught Place junction to Ramlila Maidan at noon. The rally at the venue is scheduled to continue from 10am to 5pm.INDIA bloc leaders are expected to travel in open buses from Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's residence to the march's starting point.The protest is expected to bring together leaders and supporters of opposition parties, along with student groups and civil society organisations.The INDIA bloc has appealed to students, youth, women and workers to participate.The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), founded by Abhijeet Dipke, and several student organisations have also extended support to the mobilisation.While INDIA bloc leaders have projected a turnout of up to 10 lakh, Delhi Police expects around 50,000 people. Officials estimate that the ground can accommodate 45,000 to 50,000 people when empty, news agency PTI reported. With chairs, enclosures and passageways in place, its capacity is expected to fall to around 30,000 to 40,000. Additional space will be kept outside to manage any spillover.More than 4,000 police personnel, along with Central Armed Police Forces companies, will be deployed along the march route and at the venue. Ramlila Maidan has been divided into 14 security zones, each supervised by an assistant commissioner of police-rank officer.More than 200 CCTV cameras, drones and body-worn cameras will be used for surveillance. A control room has also been set up inside the ground to monitor the arrangements.Traffic restrictions will remain in force across parts of Delhi between 10am and 5pm. Diversions are planned at major intersections, including ITO, Delhi Gate, Rajghat, Ajmeri Gate and Turkman Gate. Commuters have been advised to avoid Bahadur Shah Zafar Marg, Jawaharlal Nehru Marg, Minto Road and Desh Bandhu Gupta Road.Special arrangements will be made to ensure that ambulances and emergency vehicles can reach LNJP and GB Pant hospitals. Passengers travelling to New Delhi Railway Station have also been advised to plan their journeys in advance.Delhi Police has said permission has been granted for the rally at Ramlila Maidan, but it has not received an application for the proposed procession from the Minto Road-Connaught Place junction.The rally follows a symbolic 'public impeachment' of Kumar organised by the INDIA bloc at Kharge's residence on Saturday. Former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar presided over the proceedings, while Kharge moved a resolution listing the opposition's allegations against the CEC. Rahul Gandhi delivered the concluding remarks before the resolution was adopted.Leaders of opposition parties, civil society representatives and people affected by the SIR exercise participated in the proceedings, which were modelled on parliamentary debates.The resolution accused Kumar of facilitating alleged electoral manipulation, large-scale deletion of voters and undermining the Election Commission's independence, and called for his removal.
Article Summary: Opposition parties to hold anti-CEC rally at Ramlila Maidan on Sunday. Opposition parties expect a turnout of up to 10 lakh people. Police deploying more than 4,000 personnel to manage security and crowds. 200 CCTV cameras, drones and body-worn cameras will be used for surveillance.

EKTA NAGAR, KEVADIA: PM Narendra Modi Saturday attacked opposition for abandoning its constitutional duty and instead resorting to politics of ‘obstruction’, driven by “despair and disappointment”. Addressing the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas parade — organised annually on the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel — Modi recalled how Sardar Patel and BR Ambedkar had, while framing the Constitution, clearly laid down duties and roles of govt and opposition.“Opposition is exercising politics of ‘obstruction’, in complete disregard of constitutional boundaries and propriety,” he added.Warning against divisive forces that have come out in the open after more than a decade of political frustration to plot conspiracies, pit citizens against one another, and weaponise social media to spread rumours and tarnish India’s image, the PM urged citizens to recognise the patterns of such forces conducting secret foreign meetings, their external backing by anti-India elements, and their rhetoric echoing the nation’s enemies. “We have ended Naxalism in remote areas, but the threat from ideological extremists (dimagi Naxals) is not yet over, and the country has to remain ever vigilant against such entities,” he cautioned.Stressing that the grand mission of national unity and the journey toward a strong and capable India must continue regardless of difficulties, the PM outlined the next major national priorities of fully securing India’s borders, putting an end to infiltration and resulting demographic changes, and advancing toward a secular civil code.Acknowledging that major resolutions and bold decisions will inevitably face roadblocks and storms, he declared that the nation will not be deterred from the unwavering resolves of ‘Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat’ and a ‘Viksit Bharat’, working tirelessly with every breath and heartbeat toward the 2047 goal of a strong and capable India.Modi also referred to the instability and uncertainty facing the world in the current times, with some countries at war and major nations facing global supply chain disruptions and energy crises, while also recalling how India beat apprehensions that it would be among the worst affected by energy crisis. "Amid these apprehensions, some anti-india forces had also become active. But thanks to India's resilience, we did not let the people feel the hit of global energy crisis. This is a diplomatic and political victory of India…as well of the unity of its people," he stated.The prime minister, while attacking the earlier govt of electorally milking the promise of 'garibi hatao' without delivering on it, cited a recent World Bank report that stated that 50 crore Indians had beaten poverty over the past 10-12 year preceding 2024.Recalling that he had last year, while paying homage at the 'Statue of Unity', resolved not to rest until the country became Naxal-free, the prime minister said the goal has been achieved in the next one year. I"n 2015, 126 districts were Naxal-hit. By March 2026, not a single district was Naxal-hit. For decades, youths there who once faced an uncertain future, now have access to opportunities like education and employment," he said."In this parade, families of Naxal-hit areas are invited. I welcome them and hope for their bright future. I also salute the security personnel who made the supreme sacrifice to restore peace in the once Naxal-hit states," said the prime minister.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi attacked opposition for abandoning its constitutional duty and instead resorting to politics of ‘obstruction’ Addressing the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas parade — organised annually on the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. PM said the next major priority is fully securing India’s borders.

Article Title: ‘Don’t just protest, shop’: Rahul urges INDIA bloc rally to support Delhi traders

Rahul Gandhi urges protesters to shop

Traders flag festive-season business losses

NEW DELHI: As thousands of people gathered at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi on Sunday for the INDIA bloc’s ‘Chalo Dilli’ rally, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi urged participants to support local traders by shopping from their stores during the festive season. His appeal came after traders’ associations opposed the November 1 rally, warning that the gathering could disrupt business in the capital’s key commercial markets.In a video message posted on X late on Saturday, Gandhi appealed to people travelling to Delhi from different parts of the country to support small businesses by purchasing goods after attending the rally. He said the gathering would not hurt traders and accused the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of spreading rumours about its economic impact.“Tomorrow, lakhs of people are coming to Delhi for the Ramlila March. It is the festive season. The time of Diwali, Chhath, and Bhai Dooj has arrived. I want those lakhs of people coming to Delhi from outside to support the traders here,” Gandhi said.“Protest, march, hold rallies, and along with that, do a little shopping too - it will benefit the traders,” he added.Reiterating his appeal, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha said: “I know the rally will not harm the traders.The BJP is scared, that's why it's spreading rumours.”“But let's do both. Tomorrow there will be a march, there will be a rally, and lakhs of people will buy goods from the small shops of our traders,” he said, while extending Diwali greetings.Gandhi's appeal follows representations by the Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) and the Federation of Sadar Bazar Traders Association, which had urged him and Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi to defer the November 1 rally until after the festive season.In its letter, CTI warned that an estimated 10 lakh participants and 15,000-20,000 vehicles could trigger severe traffic congestion across central Delhi's commercial markets.“We demand to reschedule the mega-rally of 1 million (10 lakh) people, planned for November 1, to a date after Diwali; lack of parking for 15,000–20,000 vehicles could lead to a total gridlock, akin to a lockdown,” the traders' body said.The Federation of Sadar Bazar Traders Association also highlighted the financial stakes, stating that the period from Dhanteras to Diwali accounts for an estimated business turnover of around Rs 25,000 crore. It warned that disruption could affect shopkeepers, workers, delivery personnel and other people dependent on the festive trade.The association urged Rahul to take up the concerns of Delhi’s trading community with the Congress leadership and seek a postponement of the rally until after November 10, so businesses could complete their festive-season operations without disruption.The INDIA bloc rally, however, is being held at Ramlila Maidan against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Protesters gathering at the venue have raised slogans including “Vote chor, gaddi chhod”, demanding accountability over alleged electoral irregularities.

Gandhi appealed to people travelling to Delhi from different parts of the country to support small businesses by purchasing goods after attending the rally.

SRINAGAR: J&K CM Omar Abdullah faces a growing revolt within National Conference (NC), with around 25 legislators demanding replacement of all eight cabinet ministers, including the deputy CM, within 15 days and removal of his close aide and political adviser Nasir Aslam Wani.At a meeting at NC MLA Qaiser Jamshaid Lone’s home Friday evening, legislators passed a resolution seeking a cabinet overhaul and wider consultations within the party before portfolios are allocated. Around 18 MLAs attended in person and seven joined online, according to a legislator who was present. NC has 41 MLAs in 90-member assembly and runs a coalition govt with six Congress, six independent and one CPM legislator.“So far there is no next step. The first step was a big step to bring democracy within the party,” the legislator said. The resolution sought removal of all eight ministers and Wani for the “larger good of the party”.NC provincial president for Kashmir Showkat Mir confirmed the meeting but played down its significance, saying it was not directed against the party. He said some senior legislators wanted an appointment with NC president Farooq Abdullah.“Everyone wants to become a minister but the CM can appoint only eight in UT set up,” Mir said, adding that 24 legislators could be accommodated in the cabinet if statehood was restored.Omar, 56, and his father Farooq Abdullah are in New Delhi, where the CM celebrated his wedding with journalist Nidhi Razdan. Sharing a photograph on social media, Omar wrote: “A new journey began yesterday.” On July 31, Supreme Court granted Omar a divorce after being informed that he and his estranged wife Payal Abdullah had settled their matrimonial dispute through mediation.The NC turmoil came as party MP Aga Ruhullah Mehdi prepared to quit the party and surrender his Lok Sabha seat on Nov 3, accusing Omar and his ministers of betraying the party’s promises on restoration of Article 370 and protection of J&K’s rights.“The crown prince and his cabal treat J&K as an estate passed down through the family,” Mehdi wrote on X. He accused NC of seeking votes on promises to restore Article 370 and release prisoners, only to abandon them after assuming office.Mehdi will address people at Budgam on Nov 3, the death anniversary of his father Aga Syed Mehdi, a Congress politician and prominent Shiite cleric assassinated in a terrorist attack on Nov 3, 2000. Mehdi has been among Omar’s sharpest critics, accusing him of abandoning NC’s manifesto.The MLAs’ meeting followed Omar’s cabinet expansion last week, triggering open dissent, protests and allegations of internal bias in NC after four ministers were inducted, taking the cabinet’s strength to nine, including the CM. He dropped Satish Sharma, leaving only two ministers from Jammu region — deputy CM Surinder Choudhary and Javed Ahmed Rana.BJP has predicted a split in NC and collapse of Omar’s govt. “I am telling you there is unrest against the party brass. They are looking for an alternative. Govt will not remain and the party will not remain,” leader of opposition Sunil Sharma said. He described Omar as a “prince, who doesn’t want to listen to any legislator”.
Article Summary: Around 25 NC legislators have sought a cabinet overhaul and the removal of Omar Abdullah’s political adviser, exposing growing discontent within the ruling party. The resolution sought removal of all eight ministers and Wani for the ‘larger good of the party’

Article Title: The great Indian railway upgrade: How much has really changed for passengers?
Article Text:
Bigger stations, better trains: Is the passenger experience keeping pace?

A makeover on a massive scale

From station facelifts to faster trains: Inside Indian Railways' makeover

New trains, new expectations

The basic amenities test

Railway modernisation vs ground reality: The widening passenger amenities gap

Cleanliness does not end at the platform

Punctuality: Progress, but not the whole picture

Crowds are an infrastructure problem, too

Vande Bharat sees 34% rise in passengers: Is the network ready for more?

From construction to service delivery

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: New trains, redeveloped stations and upgraded infrastructure are changing the face of Indian Railways. But has the passenger experience changed at the same pace?For millions of people who depend on the network every day, the real test of modernisation begins well beyond a station's new facade or a train's sleek exterior. It lies in whether platforms are manageable, toilets are clean, drinking water is safe, coaches are well maintained and trains arrive on time.While the Railways has invested heavily in modernisation, government audits continue to flag gaps in basic passenger amenities, onboard cleanliness and maintenance. The contrast raises a larger question: Is Indian Railways building a more modern network without doing enough to improve the everyday journey?The challenge now is to ensure that the transformation is felt not just in the infrastructure passengers see, but in the quality of service they experience.The Amrit Bharat Station Scheme is among the most visible parts of the railway modernisation drive. Under the scheme, 1,337 stations had been identified for redevelopment by December 2025, with work completed at 155 stations at that point, according to the ministry of railways. The programme envisages improvements to station buildings, waiting halls, toilets, seating, drinking-water facilities, platforms, foot overbridges, lifts, escalators and passenger information systems.The plan also seeks to improve access to stations, connect them better with the surrounding city and integrate different modes of transport. Facilities for passengers with disabilities and spaces for local products under the One Station One Product initiative are part of the wider approach. The idea is to make stations more accessible and useful, rather than treat redevelopment as a cosmetic exercise alone.The scale of the programme matters in a network where stations serve very different kinds of traffic. A major city terminal may need to handle large crowds, multiple platforms and complex interchange movements. A smaller station may need reliable drinking water, sufficient seating, accessible toilets and a safe way to cross between platforms. A uniform-looking makeover cannot substitute for facilities suited to the number and needs of passengers using each station.Redevelopment also has to take place while trains continue to run. Railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw has cited the difficulty of carrying out major construction without shutting down busy stations. Work near operational tracks, shifting utilities, statutory clearances and restrictions imposed to protect passengers and train movements can all affect project schedules.That is a reminder that infrastructure transformation takes time. It also raises a separate question: While construction continues, how effectively are existing facilities being maintained?The train itself is another important part of the modernisation story. Vande Bharat has become the most recognisable symbol of a more contemporary railway experience, with modern coaches, improved passenger amenities and a focus on faster intercity travel.The demand for these services has been substantial. The ministry of railways said nearly 3.98 crore passengers travelled on Vande Bharat Express services in 2025-26, up from 2.97 crore in 2024-25, an increase of about 34%. Since its introduction, the service had carried more than 9.1 crore passengers through approximately one lakh trips, according to a ministry statement issued in April 2026.The appeal is understandable. Modern coaches, comfortable seating and onboard amenities can make a long journey less tiring. Faster services can also help passengers who travel regularly for work, education, business or family commitments. The introduction of a sleeper version in January 2026 extended the modern-train push to overnight travel. In its first three months, the sleeper service carried 1.21 lakh passengers over 119 trips, with reported occupancy exceeding 100%.A railway official, speaking to TOI on condition of anonymity, said the introduction of newer trains was part of a broader effort to improve passenger facilities.“New trains such as Vande Bharat and Amrit Bharat are being introduced using push-pull technology, offering passengers improved facilities. The work undertaken over the past few years is gradually beginning to show results,” the official said.These figures indicate that passengers are willing to use newer services when they offer a compelling travel option. But the success of a premium service should not become the sole measure of progress across a network that serves passengers with widely differing budgets and travel needs.For a family travelling in a reserved sleeper coach, the condition of the toilets and availability of water may matter as much as the train's design. For an unreserved passenger, access to a platform without dangerous crowding may be the more immediate concern. For someone travelling with an elderly relative, working lifts and clear signage can make the difference between a manageable journey and a stressful one.The next phase of modernisation must therefore be about raising the baseline across the network, not just creating pockets of premium travel.A Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) audit provides a sobering measure of the gap between infrastructure ambitions and everyday facilities. Its Report No. 31 of 2026, tabled in Parliament on August 12, examined passenger amenities and sanitation at non-suburban railway stations. Of the 512 stations covered, 458 had deficiencies in one or more essential passenger amenities.According to the CAG report, the deficiencies involved basic facilities such as toilets, urinals and drinking water. The audit also found E. coli contamination in water samples collected from coolers at eight locations, raising concerns about the safety of drinking water available to passengers.These findings matter because the usefulness of a facility depends on more than its installation. A water cooler may appear on a station's list of amenities, but it serves little purpose if the water is unsafe or the equipment is not maintained. A newly built toilet is not a meaningful improvement if it is dirty, lacks water or is routinely out of order.The distinction between providing an amenity and delivering a functioning service is central to the passenger experience. Construction can be measured through expenditure, project completion and the number of facilities created. Maintenance is less dramatic, but it determines whether passengers can actually use those facilities on a particular day.The CAG findings do not mean every station performs poorly, nor do they erase the benefits of redevelopment. They point instead to unevenness across the network. The task is to ensure that passengers do not have to depend on a station's size, location or level of visibility to access basic services.The problem extends from stations to the trains themselves. A separate CAG audit on cleanliness and sanitation in long-distance trains, covering the period from 2018-19 to 2022-23, found that more than 40% of surveyed passengers were dissatisfied with toilet cleanliness, while over half expressed dissatisfaction with onboard housekeeping.The survey covered 2,426 passengers across 96 selected trains. The audit identified issues including dirty lavatories, choked washbasins, waterlogging and unclean vestibules. It also found that 366 passengers, or about 15% of those surveyed, reported a lack of water in toilets or washbasins. More than one lakh complaints about water shortages in train toilets and washbasins were registered through Rail Madad in 2022-23.The audit also highlighted shortcomings in the deployment of cleaning staff and equipment, as well as gaps in monitoring and enforcement of contractual obligations. It mentioned that 89% of complaints related to toilet cleanliness were addressed within the stipulated timeframe. That points to a system capable of responding to complaints, but also to the need to reduce the conditions that generate them in the first place.The railway official said bio-toilets had played an important role in the effort to improve sanitation, but maintenance and passenger awareness remained challenges.“Indian Railways has taken extensive measures to improve cleanliness, with bio-toilets playing an important role in this effort. However, the key challenge lies in their adequate maintenance, due to which problems continue to arise. Lack of awareness among passengers also contributes to sanitation-related issues,” the official said.“Although the Railways is working to spread awareness through advertisements and other means, a change in public attitude towards cleanliness is still needed,” the official added.A complaint mechanism is essential. Yet a passenger should not have to repeatedly report a choked toilet or an empty water tank for routine services to be delivered. Onboard housekeeping, water refilling and regular inspections need to work as part of normal railway operations, not only after a problem has been flagged.Cleanliness is not a minor comfort issue. It affects dignity, health and the willingness of passengers to trust the service. A train can have modern coaches and advanced safety features, but if the washroom becomes unusable halfway through a long journey, the experience quickly falls short of the promise.Reliability is another test of whether the passenger experience is keeping pace with infrastructure investment. A faster train is useful only if its schedule is dependable, while an upgraded station cannot compensate for a journey that routinely runs late.The ministry of railways reported that punctuality improved from 73.62% in 2023-24 to 77.12% in 2024-25, reaching 77.24% in 2025-26 up to February 2026. The ministry said the network operates around 25,000 trains a day and attributed delays to a range of factors, including fog, track and route constraints, maintenance, signalling issues, agitations and other unforeseen events.The improvement is significant, but the latest figure also shows that punctuality remains a work in progress. Railway operations involve a vast network in which a disruption in one section can affect services elsewhere. Track maintenance, signalling upgrades and other work may be necessary to improve long-term reliability, even when they cause short-term inconvenience.The railway official said the growing demand for passenger trains had put pressure on punctuality, and that infrastructure upgrades were being undertaken to address the issue.“To address this, the Railways has started operating dedicated freight corridors or undertaken work on them to provide separate tracks for goods trains. The Delhi-Mumbai Dedicated Freight Corridor is a key example,” the official said.“Major stations are also undergoing remodelling and interlocking work to reduce additional halts and delays for trains. Sections with heavy traffic are being converted to automatic signalling systems,” the official added.The official said fog and mist also affected train operations by reducing visibility. “To address this, fog signal devices have been installed in locomotives. In addition, the Railways is installing the advanced Kavach system, which not only helps improve punctuality but also plays an important role in ensuring train safety,” the official said.For passengers, however, the experience is immediate. A late train can mean a missed connection, a longer wait at a station or an uncertain arrival time. Better information about delays and platform changes can ease some of that burden, but communication cannot replace reliable operations.More dependable schedules, clear announcements, accurate digital information and prompt assistance during disruptions are as important to many travellers as the design of the coach.Crowd management has become another part of the passenger experience that cannot be separated from station design. Wider foot overbridges, holding areas, better access points and clearer passenger information can help manage movement, but they need to be matched to actual footfall and train capacity.The New Delhi railway station witnessed a stampede in February 2025 that killed at least 18 people.In March 2026, the railway ministry announced plans for permanent holding areas at 76 identified stations, alongside measures including access control, wider foot overbridges and technology-assisted monitoring. The ministry also referred to additional ticketing facilities, drinking-water arrangements and separate toilets at New Delhi Railway Station.The railway official said satellite stations were being developed in large and industrial cities to reduce pressure on major stations during periods of heavy passenger movement.“In large and industrial cities, where passenger footfall rises sharply during holidays and other occasions, the Railways has started developing satellite stations to reduce the pressure on major stations,” the official said.The official also referred to the Train on Demand initiative, particularly services with high-capacity unreserved coaches, to accommodate more passengers through fewer trains.Such measures recognise that a station is not simply a building through which passengers pass. It is a space where thousands of people may arrive at the same time, often carrying luggage, travelling with children or trying to reach a platform minutes before departure.But crowd management cannot depend on temporary arrangements alone. It also requires better coordination between train schedules, platform allocation, ticketing, station staff and the movement of people inside and outside the premises. The test is whether a passenger can reach the right platform safely and without confusion, particularly during holiday rushes, festivals and other peak periods.A station's success should not be judged only by its appearance when relatively empty. Its real test comes when several trains arrive close together and thousands of passengers have to move through the same spaces.The larger question facing Indian Railways is how to turn a massive modernisation programme into a consistently better everyday service. The answer lies partly in investment, but also in maintenance, staffing, monitoring and accountability.The government has committed substantial resources to passenger amenities. In December 2025, the ministry said an allocation of Rs 12,118 crore had been made under the customer amenities budget head for 2025-26, with Rs 7,253 crore spent up to October that year. Such spending can create the physical conditions for better journeys. Whether it produces lasting improvement depends on how effectively facilities are operated and maintained.There is no single measure that captures the passenger experience. Station redevelopment figures tell us how much work has been undertaken. New-train numbers indicate the expansion of services. Punctuality statistics measure one aspect of reliability. Audit findings reveal whether basic facilities meet the expected standard. Together, they offer a more complete picture than any one headline figure.A meaningful assessment would ask how many station amenities remain functional, whether drinking water is safe, how often toilets are cleaned, whether complaints are resolved promptly, and how consistently trains run to schedule. It would also compare performance across stations and railway zones, so that strong results in one area do not conceal persistent gaps elsewhere.Indian Railways has good reason to invest in bigger stations, modern trains and improved infrastructure. For a country of India's size, rail travel remains essential to mobility, livelihoods and social connection. The scale of the network makes the task difficult, but it also makes the quality of everyday service especially important.The next measure of progress should be visible not just in the station's new facade or the train's sleek exterior, but in the ordinary details of a journey: A clean washroom, safe water, a working lift, a manageable platform and a train that arrives when expected.
Article Summary: The real test of modernisation begins well beyond a station's new facade or a train's sleek exterior. It lies in whether platforms are manageable, toilets are clean, drinking water is safe, coaches are well maintained and trains arrive on time. Government audits continue to flag gaps in basic passenger amenities, onboard cleanliness and maintenance.

Article Title: ‘Water ingress’ incident on Navy vessel, no casualties reported
Article Text:
Water entered INS Kesari while it was berthed at Visakhapatnam’s Naval Dockyard, with the Navy reporting no casualties and dewatering efforts underway

NEW DELHI: The Indian Navy on Saturday confirmed an incident of “water ingress” (flooding) on one of its ships while the vessel was berthed at the Naval Dockyard in Visakhapatnam . The incident was reported on INS Kesari, a Shardul-class tank landing ship.The Navy, in an official statement, said that “no casualties have been reported”. Efforts to pump out the water are underway, it added.INS Kesari, which was commissioned on April 5, 2008, has a 5,650-tonne displacement.Deployed in May 2020 for Mission Sagar, INS Kesari had delivered Covid-19 relief material, medical assistance and food items to nations in the southern Indian Ocean, such as Maldives, Mauritius, Madagascar, Comoros and Seychelles.
Article Summary: Water entered INS Kesari while it was berthed at Visakhapatnam’s Naval Dockyard. The Navy, in an official statement, said that “no casualties have been reported’ Efforts to pump out the water are underway, it added.
