Article Title: 'Will deal with Modi, Shah': Rahul Gandhi explains why CEC Gyanesh Kumar is his first target
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi warned the CEC and other officials against assuming that constitutional immunity would shield them from accountability.

'We are not going to let you escape'

INDIA bloc holds 'public impeachment' of CEC

BJP calls it 'mockery' of democracy

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah may be at the top of the political chain of command, but Rahul Gandhi has made it clear that the opposition's first target is Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.Explaining why the INDIA bloc has upped its attack on the election chief, the Congress leader accused him of acting as an instrument of the ruling establishment and warned that those allegedly involved in undermining democratic institutions would be held accountable."Mr Modi and Mr Shah might be on top. We will deal with them, but you are their instruments, and so you are our first target," Rahul Gandhi said on Saturday at the INDIA bloc event in Delhi, where opposition leaders held a symbolic public impeachment of Gyanesh Kumar.The leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha warned the CEC and other officials against assuming that constitutional immunity would shield them from accountability."So if Mr Gyanesh Kumar thinks, or the five or seven people below him think, that immunity will save them, I would kindly suggest to them, with love and affection, to take a look at what is going on in the country. Please understand the mood of the people outside.You will see tomorrow itself," he said.Rahul Gandhi was referring to the opposition's planned march and public rally in Delhi on Sunday, which he described as an opportunity for a united opposition to demonstrate public anger over alleged electoral irregularities."A united opposition is going to show you exactly what the mood of the people of this country is," he said.Rahul Gandhi said the opposition's action against CEC was not an isolated protest against one constitutional functionary but part of a larger fight over what he alleged was the misuse of democratic institutions."You can continue to rig the elections. You can continue to control and allow the misuse of the CBI, the ED, and every single institution of this country. But we guarantee you that this is a temporary phenomenon," he said.The Congress leader insisted that Gyanesh Kumar was only one among several people the opposition held responsible for what it described as an assault on the country's democratic institutions."We are not going to let you escape. I also want to address the people who have carried out this assault on the Union of India. Gyanesh Kumar is just one element; there are many others. We know who they are, and we understand deeply who they are," Rahul Gandhi said."This is a warning to you: things are shifting. Please hear this warning and realise that this is a new political weapon sitting in the garden, and this weapon is going to hurt you very badly if you continue down your path," he said."I am saying this with love and affection; we are not nasty or evil people, but we will protect the Constitution and the voice of our people."Rahul Gandhi also backed the demand for legal action against the CEC, saying Gyanesh Kumar should not only face impeachment but also be tried in court for treason."I fully support the motion that Mr Gyanesh Kumar should not only be impeached but should also be tried in a court of law for treason so that justice can be served," he said.Rahul Gandhi's remarks came at an unprecedented INDIA bloc event in which opposition MPs and leaders, along with civil society representatives, passed a resolution seeking Gyanesh Kumar's impeachment and accusing him of facilitating the deletion of voters' names to influence election outcomes.The symbolic proceedings were held at the lawns of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's residence at 10, Rajaji Marg in New Delhi. Former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar presided over the meeting, which was organised in a setting resembling parliamentary proceedings.The resolution was moved by Kharge, seconded by Samajwadi Party leader Harendra Malik and supported by Rahul Gandhi and several other opposition MPs and civil society members. It was adopted unanimously by a show of hands.Around 250 opposition MPs, civil society representatives and mediapersons attended the event. Some people who alleged that their names had been wrongly deleted from electoral rolls were also present.Rahul Gandhi acknowledged that holding what resembled parliamentary proceedings outside Parliament might appear unusual, but said the opposition had been left with little choice."I don't think anything like this has ever happened in history," he said, adding that the gathering of opposition leaders and civil society members in a garden might appear absurd."But we had no other option, as every single institution is closed to us," he said.The stage was designed to resemble the old Lok Sabha chamber, with a wooden-panelled backdrop and seats arranged in a semi-circular formation.Kharge, who moved the motion, alleged that the right to vote was under threat because the Election Commission was functioning at the behest of PM Modi and Shah. He accused the poll panel of failing to act independently and raised concerns over alleged electoral manipulation.The BJP hit back at the opposition's symbolic proceedings, accusing the INDIA bloc of making a mockery of Parliament and democratic institutions.BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra took a swipe at Rahul Gandhi, alleging that the Congress was repeatedly attempting to launch its leader politically without success."Go ahead and hold your mock Parliament or take out your marches; the world has already understood that Rahul Gandhi simply lacks the fuel. This 'satellite' is never going to launch," Patra said.He added that the opposition could have Gandhi as a "mock Prime Minister for life".
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi warns the CEC and other officials against assuming that constitutional immunity would shield them from accountability. Opposition leaders hold symbolic public impeachment of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Gandhi backs demand for legal action against CEC, saying he should also be tried in court for treason.

Article Title: Uttarakhand helicopter crash reiterates concerns raised by Parliamentary panel
Article Text:
Another Char Dham chopper crash revives concerns over aviation safety lapses flagged by a parliamentary panel

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Yet another crash of a chopper ferrying pilgrims on the Char Dham route has brought into focus safety flags raised by a parliamentary panel overseeing aviation sector that have gone unheeded despite recurring tragedies.From "responsibility vacuum" which dilutes accountability to "pressure culture" that allows commercial considerations to override no-go weather conditions, the committee has in its recent reports, including one in March, highlighted several worrying factors at play in the helicopter services being offered to Char Dham pilgrims."The situation with helicopter operations in Char Dham sector is a symptom of a larger and dangerous structural flaw in India's aviation governance: a fractured and ambiguous regulatory command structure," the parliamentary panel on transport, tourism and culture headed by JDU MP Sanjay Jha had said.It said DGCA has ceded direct oversight of one of the country's most hazardous aviation zones to a state-level body, Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority, whose capacity and expertise are under the scanner. This two-tiered safety system, with differing levels of scrutiny, is inherently unsafe and unsustainable, it added.A series of chopper crashes on the Char Dham route last year had led the committee to consult a number of experts and stakeholders, including aviation ministry, DGCA and private players, to look into the reasons behind the accidents and offer recommendations which, sources said, are yet to be implemented.The committee also pointed out "a glaring regulatory gap of significant concern", which is the absence of any mandatory, terrain-specific mountain flying training and certification for pilots who operate in the treacherous Himalayan region. "DGCA itself had expressed concern that UCADA lacked adequately trained and competent manpower for such high-density operations, yet a specific training mandate for these unique conditions was not in place.Aviation ministry acknowledged the high-risk operational environment, marked by challenging topography, rapidly changing and often severe climatic conditions, and high-density traffic, and said the inherent risks warranted immediate and serious intervention.
Article Summary: A series of chopper crashes on the Char Dham route last year had led the committee to consult a number of experts and stakeholders. The committee also pointed out "a glaring regulatory gap of significant concern", which is the absence of any mandatory, terrain-specific mountain flying training and certification for pilots.

Article Title: Haunted, but hardly explored: India's untapped ghost-tourism economy
Article Text:
India’s haunted destinations offer an untapped tourism opportunity, with paranormal experiences yet to become a mainstream travel attraction. (AI-generated image)

The business of the macabre

From a haunted reputation to a tourism product

The business of making a place come alive

Ghost is only part of the experience

Local community cannot remain part of the backdrop

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India's ghosts have a customer service problem.There is almost an abundance of local places which have a reputation of being haunted in each and every state.There are ghost villages where nobody is quite sure why everyone left. Forts with stories of spirits walking through them at night. Abandoned cemeteries as old as the world wars, forgotten ‘havelis’ and stretches of forest that have acquired a mythology of their own.Out of all these only a few have become tourist attractions; others survive largely through word of mouth, local lore and the occasional paranormal investigation.India's haunted places do have an audience but it somehow lacks a concrete machinery that could make ‘dark’ tourism and ‘spectral’ cities central factions of an ever growing tourist economy.The tourism industry has a name for this particular appetite for the unsettling: dark tourism. The term broadly describes travel to places associated with death, tragedy, violence and suffering.Ghost tours, haunted heritage walks and visits to places associated with paranormal folklore occupy a more specialised corner of this spectrum, where history, local legend and the promise of an eerie experience often intersect.It is an appetite that the tourism industry has increasingly tried to package. Turning a city's darker history into something you can book online. And its most ideal form, the ticket buys you a completely immersive tour full of storytelling with a slight hope of encountering your first paranormal spirit.The commercial potential of dark tourism is reflected in the market estimates. Grand View Research valued the global dark tourism market at $31.8 billion in 2023 and projects it to reach $34.2 billion in 2026 and $38.6 billion by 2030, growing at a compound annual growth rate of 2.9%. MR puts the market at $32 billion in 2025, forecasting it to reach $46.8 billion by 2036.The market for ghost tourism as a separate entity is estimated to be worth $2.9 billion in 2025 and projects it to grow to $5.7 billion by 2034, at a CAGR of 7.8%, by Dataintelo. Its estimate includes guided ghost walks, cemetery and underground tours, paranormal investigations, haunted stays and virtual experiences.For India, the more immediate question may be less about capturing a share of a global market and more about whether these scattered attractions can be turned into viable profitable local experiences. With a history as rich as ours, the ghosts are not in short supply. The challenge is to turn them into profitable experiences that people can discover, book and pay for, while ensuring that the tragedy is respected and the communities living alongside these places have a stake in the business.Kuldhara, a site that Rajasthan Tourism itself promotes as a “ghost village shrouded in mystery”, is a good starting point. The official government site describes its history as a prosperous settlement abandoned in the early 19th century. The account recounts the popular legend involving the village headman's daughter and the powerful minister Salim Singh, while also identifying the ruins as a protected monument under the state archaeology department.The village, around 17km from Jaisalmer, already has the ingredients of a tourism attraction, but having a story and having a well-managed visitor experience are two different things.There are multiple accounts of litter around the site, including discarded plastic and food packaging. How can an atmosphere feel haunted when the landscape is strewn with chips and tobacco packets?And cleanliness isn’t the only issue. Talking to two people who visited the site, the common experience has been mismanaged and under researched tour which leaves most customers underwhelmed at the end of the day.Bhangarh, in Alwar district, is often described as one of India's most haunted places. Rajasthan Tourism itself recounts the two popular legends attached to the site: one involving the ascetic Baba Balu Nath, whose warning about the shadow of the fort was allegedly ignored, and another about a sorcerer whose failed attempt to enchant Princess Ratnavati supposedly led him to curse the town.The legends have become part of the destination's appeal, drawing visitors to its ruined temples, palaces and deserted marketplace. The restriction on entry before sunrise and after sunset, imposed at the site, has only added to its mystique. But tourists who visit the site have also called it unorganised, speaking to TOI they noted that the guide also was not entirely accurate about the historical aspects of the site and the site itself needed to have better management.There are already attempts to package India's haunted heritage into guided experiences. Delhi Tourism lists Haunted Heritage Walks at Malcha Mahal and Feroz Shah Kotla Monument, each lasting around 90 minutes and available on weekends on group demand. The official booking page lists a minimum group size of six and a tariff of Rs 800 plus GST per person.The Ministry of Tourism's Utsav portal has also listed a Haunted Walk at Bhuli Bhatiyari, organised by Delhi-based Enroute Indian History. The listing describes a guided heritage walk through the old hunting lodge, combining its history with the legends associated with the site.Enroute Indian History, which has been conducting the experience for around two to three years, says the walks attract a good number of bookings and are designed for adventure seekers as much as for history enthusiasts. The operator says it takes care to keep the historical information accurate, while folklore and supernatural accounts are presented as stories rather than fact-checked historical claims. This distinction is central to the format: visitors are offered a combination of documented history, local legends and the possibility of an unsettling experience.These initiatives complicate the idea that haunted tourism in India is entirely informal or absent. There are government-backed products and private operators working in the space. The question is whether they have developed the consistency, visibility and scale needed to make haunted experiences a dependable part of a destination's tourism economy.Detailing her experience to TOI, Kriti notes that she remembers the underground setting of the haunted heritage walk she took in Edinburgh as much as the stories themselves. The interactive displays and historical details provided by the guide gave the experience a sense of depth that a conventional ghost walk might not have offered.A ghost tour can take several forms, the attraction lies as much in how visitors encounter the story as in the story itself.A 2020 study published in Cornell Hospitality Quarterly, titled Paranormal Tourism: Market Study of a Novel and Interactive Approach to Space Activation and Monetization, makes this case through examples from the United States and elsewhere. It describes how destinations such as New Orleans combine ghost stories with local histories and cultural associations, while Salem packages its reputation around witches and ghosts. These places do not necessarily sell a standalone encounter with the paranormal; they draw on identities and histories that visitors may already associate with them.The study talks in detail about Eastern State Penitentiary in Philadelphia, a former prison that closed in 1971 and subsequently fell into disuse. Limited group tours began in 1988 as part of efforts to preserve the site. A Halloween fundraiser followed in 1991, eventually developing into the annual attraction Terror Behind the Walls. By 1994, the former prison was also offering daily historical tours to generate income for preservation, followed by museum exhibits and a broader marketing campaign.The study also points to the role of participation in making these experiences engaging. The experience can continue beyond the visit itself, with reviews, photographs and word of mouth helping to draw in new audiences.Research into British ghost walks suggests that the appeal is not necessarily dependent on visitors believing in ghosts. An ethnographic study of 14 tours across Edinburgh, York, London and Brighton found that guides use a combination of storytelling, performance and the physical environment to make history tangible.For India, that distinction could be important. A haunted experience need not rely on sensational claims. It can be built around the history of a place, the folklore that has accumulated around it and the atmosphere of encountering that story on location.The opportunity, however, is not simply to make India's haunted sites more theatrical or commercially attractive. It is also to ensure that the people and places behind the stories are not left out of the value chain.A 2023 qualitative study of local perceptions in Kuldhara, based on 25 interviews with residents and people working in the area, found that respondents saw several economic opportunities in developing mystery and paranormal tourism. Some respondents also pointed to existing livelihood opportunities linked to visitors, including guiding, transport and the sale of local crafts.The study also recorded expectations around the restoration and preservation of the village, alongside concerns about the role of government and private bodies in developing the destination. While it offers a glimpse of how residents view the possibilities of mystery tourism, it does not quantify how much income currently reaches the community or how widely those benefits are distributed.The concerns are not unique to haunted destinations. A 2026 study of tourism in Uttarakhand, while not focused specifically on ghost tourism, raises wider questions about the state's tourism economy. It argues for stronger community participation, local supply chains, training and livelihood diversification.These concerns are relevant when considering how niche tourism experiences might develop in the hills. A haunted walk could create work for local storytellers, drivers, homestays, food vendors and artisans. But those benefits are not automatic. If an outside operator controls the bookings, supplies the guides and takes most of the revenue, the local community may remain little more than a feature of the landscape.The challenge is to move beyond treating local legends as raw material that can be packaged elsewhere. Residents may be the custodians of oral histories, but they should also have a stake in how those histories are interpreted and monetised.India does not need to manufacture a haunted history. What it needs is a way to bring those stories to visitors without reducing them to cheap thrills or leaving the people who have preserved them out of the business.The real test of India's haunted tourism economy will not be how many people it can convince that a place is haunted, but how many people it can persuade to stay, listen, and explore.The ghosts, after all, have been doing their bit for the tourism industry for years. It is time someone took care of the guests.
Article Summary: India's haunted places do have an audience but it lacks a concrete machinery that could make ‘dark’ tourism and ‘spectral’ cities central factions of an ever growing tourist economy. The challenge is to turn them into profitable experiences that people can discover, book and pay for, while ensuring that the tragedy is respected.

Article Title: Quad flags economic coercion, announces $85 million to expand AI access
Article Text:
Quad leaders push for resilient supply chains and greater AI access in Indo-Pacific

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Targeting China’s military and economic practices in the Indo-Pacific region, Quad foreign ministers expressed grave concerns regarding economic coercion, including through arbitrary export restrictions as well as non-market policies and practices that result in overcapacity to disrupt global supply chain in critical industries.In a meeting in Atlanta, Quad also announced plans to provide more than $ 85 million in technical and financial assistance to expand access to “trusted Super Intelligence SI” (using SI to refer to Artificial Intelligence) across the Indo-Pacific. Trump recently signed an executive order to rename AI as SI.The ministers backed ongoing cooperation on critical mineral supply chain and the need to reduce reliance on any single supplier.The foreign ministers of Australia, India, Japan and the US - Penny Wong, S Jaishankar, Toshimitsu Motegi and Marco Rubio respectively - held the 4th Quad foreign ministers’ meeting since the return of President Donald Trump to the White House last year on the margins of a G20 gathering in Atlanta Saturday.In the meeting, Motegi expressed strong opposition to any unilateral attempts to change the status quo by force or coercion even though Quad, unlike the last meeting in May, avoided mentioning South China Sea or East China Sea in the joint statement.Quad ministers have continued to meet, even as the leaders’ summit remains stalled—fueling speculation that the Trump administration has effectively downgraded the group by preventing India form hosting the event as planned.In a joint statement, the ministers reaffirmed their commitment to advancing peace, stability, and prosperity in the Indo-Pacific, as also convening of the Quad Leaders’ Summit. Rubio said after the meeting that Quad will soon announce the leaders’ summit in Manila on the margins of ASEAN meetings. President Donald Trump is scheduled to travel to China from Manila for the APEC summit.The leaders also focused on the West Asia situation including in the Strait of Hormuz.“Recognizing the importance of critical sea lanes, the uninterrupted flow of commerce, energy security, and the unhindered passage and safety of maritime crews and vessel without the imposition of tolls, they reiterated the absolute necessity to protect and preserve navigational rights and freedoms in the Strait of Hormuz, the Red Sea, and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait in accordance with international law as reflected in UNCLOS,” said the joint statement.Jaishankar said that the meeting highlighted the importance of maintaining stability, driving prosperity and ensuring freedom of choice along with deepening of clcooperation to promote supply chain resilience and ensure technology, critical minerals & energy security.He also mentioned the importance of carrying forward agreements on counter-terrorism, maritime security and capacity building to enhance resilience and contribute to peace and stability.According to the joint statement, the ministers also announced the first-ever Quad Business Leaders’ Forum that will convene industry leaders, government, and policy experts from Quad countries to foster greater ties across our public and private sectors, including the promotion of commercial deals in key sectors.“Quad countries reinforced the need to build secure, resilient, and trusted supply chains for advanced, leading-edge semiconductors and SI (AI) hardware,” said the joint statement.
Article Summary: The foreign ministers of Australia, India, Japan and the US - Penny Wong, S Jaishankar, Toshimitsu Motegi and Marco Rubio respectively - held the 4th Quad foreign ministers’ meeting since the return of President Donald Trump to the White House last year. The ministers backed ongoing cooperation on critical mineral supply chain and the need to reduce reliance on any single supplier.

Article Title: November to be slightly warmer than usual, predicts IMD
Article Text:
IMD forecasts warmer-than-usual November across most of India, with below-normal rainfall likely in much of the country and a possible cyclone bringing heavy rain to Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Nov is likely to be slightly warmer than usual, recording 'above normal' maximum (day) and minimum (night) temperatures over most parts of the country, IMD said Saturday.The Met department also predicted that the country may get 'below normal' rainfall in most parts except for some areas in central, northwest and northeast India, where normal to 'above normal' rainfall is expected in Nov. 'Below normal' rainfall may be a concern for peninsular India as that part of the country usually gets good rain during Nov on account of the winter (northeast) monsoon.The prediction of normal to 'above normal' rainfall in some areas of central and northeast India assumes significance for Madhya Pradesh and adjoining areas of Maharashtra and Gujarat, east Uttar Pradesh and Bihar as it will help wheat crop in these rain-fed regions during the month.Meanwhile, the existing depression over southwest Bay of Bengal is likely to develop as a cyclonic storm on Sunday and cross south Andhra Pradesh and north Tamil Nadu coasts during the Monday evening-Tuesday morning period, bringing heavy rain to the coastal areas of both the states. Once the existing system develops into a cyclonic storm, it will be called 'Murasu'. 'Murasu' is a Tamil word which means a drum, particularly a traditional percussion instrument."Monthly rainfall for Nov over the south Peninsular India, consisting of Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikkal, coastal Andhra Pradesh and Rayalaseema region, Kerala, Mahe and south interior Karnataka, is most likely to be 'below normal' (less than 77% of the long period average)," said IMD chief Mrutyunjay Mohapatra while releasing the monthly outlook for rainfall and temperature for Nov.The long period average of rainfall over south Peninsular India during Nov, based on data from 1971 to 2020, is 118.7 mm. In Oct, rainfall over the country (51.7 mm) was the sixth lowest since 2001 and 25th lowest since 1901, with a deficit of 31%. Rainfall over south Peninsular India (122.2 mm) was the sixth lowest since 2001.
Article Summary: IMD: Nov likely to be slightly warmer than usual, recording 'above normal' maximum (day) and minimum (night) temperatures. Met department also predicted that the country may get 'below normal' rainfall in most parts except for some areas in central, northwest and northeast India. A possible cyclone bringing heavy rain to Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.

NEW DELHI: Centre has extended the tenure of the Nandan Nilekani-led task force on examination reforms till Jan 2027, with the prime minister's office (PMO) seeking consultations with chief ministers and chief secretaries before the panel finalises its recommendations, TOI has learnt from govt officials. During consultations, some stakeholders and experts have also suggested a hybrid format for NEET-UG 2027, allowing time to expand infrastructure for a complete shift to computer-based testing (CBT) in 2028.A govt official said the PMO wants the task force, earlier expected to submit its report by Oct-end, to seek views from state leadership on challenges particular to different regions. The aim, the source said, is to better understand disparities in testing infrastructure, connectivity and administrative preparedness, and reflect these state-specific concerns in a more comprehensive examination reform roadmap.Another proposal likely to feature in the task force's recommendations is a nationwide network of CBT centres developed by Centre and state govts with private investment, sources said. Such a model could expand govt oversight of testing facilities while mobilising private capital to build infrastructure, particularly in districts that lack secure, adequately equipped centres. The funding, ownership and operating arrangements would need to be worked out.Such centres could support common security standards, reliable connectivity and better access for candidates outside metros.TOI had earlier reported that the task force is prioritising "debundling" examination responsibilities. Under the proposed restructuring, question-paper setting, conduct of exams, management of test centres and security would be assigned to separate agencies instead of being concentrated with a single operator.The objective is to create clearer lines of accountability and limit the risk of a lapse in one part of the examination process affecting the entire exercise. The approach would, however, require coordination between the agencies handling different stages.The panel is also considering exam centres in every district and a common calendar for National Testing Agency (NTA), Staff Selection Commission (SSC), Institute of Banking Personnel Selection (IBPS) and Railway Recruitment Boards (RRBs). Coordinated schedules could help students and job applicants avoid exam-date clashes and allow testing infrastructure to be used more efficiently.The six-member task force was constituted in July following the NEET-UG 2026 controversy, which led to the cancellation of the original exam and a retest. It has held 18 internal meetings and around 40 consultations, in addition to seeking public suggestions.An Oct parliamentary committee report also recommended secure govt-controlled testing centres across districts and a phased transition to CBT for NEET-UG. The extension gives the task force more time to assess the feasibility of its proposals with states.
Article Summary: Nandan Nilekani-led task force gets extension till January 2027 as exam reforms, including a possible hybrid NEET-UG format, are reviewed. PMO seeking consultations with chief ministers and chief secretaries before the panel finalises its recommendations. During consultations, some stakeholders and experts have also suggested a hybrid format.

Article Title: Authoritarianism sets in when society fears questions: Justice Bhuyan
Article Text:
‘Shun the binary of ‘us’ & ‘they’; adopt ‘we’ for unity in diversity,’ said Justice Bhuyan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: At a time when the opposition has branded the NDA govt authoritarian, Justice Ujjal Bhuyan Saturday said authoritarianism sets in when society fears questions, and stressed people must shed the binary of 'us' and 'they' and adopt the core constitutional philosophy of 'we' to preserve the country's unity in diversity.Speaking at the convocation ceremony of University of Science and Technology Meghalaya, the SC judge said, "A society that fears questions becomes vulnerable to authoritarianism. A society that treats tradition as beyond scrutiny may fail to reform unjust practices."Highlighting Article 51A of the Constitution that casts a duty on every citizen to develop a scientific temperament, Justice Bhuyan said, "It does not merely ask us to acquire scientific knowledge. It asks us to cultivate a temperament which is based on reason. It tells us to inquire, to question, to examine and, where necessary, to reform."He said, "I believe, scientific temperament lays the foundation for the rule of law. This is because arbitrary power thrives on ignorance, fear and unexamined belief. A society that accepts claims without evidence is susceptible to superstitious beliefs and becomes vulnerable to misinformation."Attaching great importance to debate, he said those who ask questions must also be willing to listen to a different point of view. "Willingness to reason together through a meaningful debate alone can make a society stronger," he said, adding that questions followed by meaningful and healthy debates can happen only when people have access to information.Inspired by Nobel laureate Amartya Sen's 'The Idea of Justice', which he quoted extensively during the speech, Justice Bhuyan elaborated on the difference between 'institutional democracy' and 'functional democracy' and said that a functional democracy requires public questioning and scrutiny. "Circulation of information and scrutiny by public reasoning thus becomes part of the due process by which a democratic society resonates with justice. "He said preservation of diversity demands shunning false narratives and the binary of 'us' and 'they'."For a more just and humane society, it is important that we move away from the destructive binary of 'us' and 'they' and embrace the idea of oneness," he said."Not for nothing, the Preamble to the Constitution starts with the expression - 'We, the People of India'. The Constitution... speaks to all citizens of India as equal members of the constitutional order. Therefore, 'we' represents a larger idea of belonging in which our individual identities or group identities do not diminish our shared constitutional unity," he said.In what could be construed as indirect opposition to Uniform Civil Code, he said, "It does not require that our individual identities should get subsumed in the larger whole. Diversity, therefore, is not an impediment to the constitutional project; rather, it infuses substance and meaning to it."
Article Summary: Justice Ujjal Bhuyan said authoritarianism sets in when society fears questions. He stressed people must shed the binary of 'us' and 'they' and adopt 'we' to preserve the country's unity in diversity. He was speaking at convocation ceremony of University of Science and Technology Meghalaya.

NEW DELHI: Union minister JP Nadda on Sunday launched a sharp attack on the Congress and Rahul Gandhi over the INDIA bloc's rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan, accusing the opposition of using the banner of democracy to create unrest, damage the economy and destabilise an elected government.Reacting to the 'Chalo Delhi' mobilisation, Nadda said the rally was a “calculated conspiracy to plunge the nation into anarchy—in the name of democracy”. He described it as a “foolish, orchestrated drama” by parties that had been defeated and rejected by voters.Addressing Rahul Gandhi directly, the Union minister outlined what he called the Congress leader's model of politics, alleging that it involved spreading misinformation, provoking street protests, harming the economy and seeking to destabilise an elected government at the behest of foreign powers.“The first stage is spreading lies and rumours; the second is inciting anarchy and chaos on the streets; the third is damaging the nation’s economy; and the fourth is attempting to destabilise an elected government at the behest of foreign powers,” Nadda said.He also alleged that the November 1 rally had four specific objectives: hurting the sentiments of the Sikh community, triggering violence in Delhi to bring down a democratically elected government, affecting the earnings of traders during the festive season and damaging India's reputation.Nadda's remarks came amid the INDIA bloc's protest against alleged irregularities in the revision of electoral rolls and its demand for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar."Rahul Gandhi, listen carefully: this is India—not some 'banana republic' where you can incite arson, trigger riots, or push an agenda for 'regime change' whenever you please. Stop dreaming, Rahul Gandhi. India is the world’s oldest and most robust democracy. November 1st stands as the most infamous and darkest stain in India’s democratic history. On this very day, goons nurtured by the Congress party massacred our innocent Sikh brethren. Thousands of Sikh families were rendered homeless overnight, and thousands of women were widowed. The nation has not forgotten; even today, the 'Widow Colony' in Delhi bears witness to that horrific and bloody chapter of Congress history. To this day, the Gandhi family has not offered a sincere apology to the Sikh community for that grave sin. Observe the insensitivity of the Congress and the petty mindset of Rahul Gandhi. On this dark day—a day when the nation ought to be remembering its martyrs and victims—Rahul Gandhi stands at Ramlila Maidan, seeking only to further his own political agenda ...", Nadda added.The rally has also drawn criticism from the BJP over its timing, with the ruling party accusing Congress of holding a political event on the anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots.BJP is holding a separate march in West Delhi under the banner of remembering the victims of the 1984 violence.The march is scheduled to proceed from Hari Nagar Bus Depot to Tilak Nagar Metro Station, with Union minister Hardeep Singh Puri, Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta, Delhi BJP president and other party leaders expected to participate.Meanwhile, the BJP and its Mahayuti allies held a 'Lokshahi Bachao, Anarajakta Hatao' (Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy) padyatra in Mumbai on Sunday.Maharashtra BJP president Ravindra Chavan accused the Congress of spreading what he described as false narratives about constitutional institutions, including the judiciary and Parliament.“At a time when the entire nation is witnessing a phase of development-oriented governance under the leadership of PM Modi, the opposition Congress party is, without any valid reason, attempting to create confusion among the public by propagating false narratives about our established institutions,” Chavan said.Shiv Sena MP Naresh Mhaske also criticised Rahul Gandhi and his associates, alleging that their activities were against the Constitution.BJP has also launched a nationwide 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' campaign to counter opposition allegations relating to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Party workers are expected to reach villages and households to present the BJP's position on the electoral process.The opposition alliance, meanwhile, has maintained that its mobilisation is aimed at protecting democratic rights and raising concerns over alleged deletions of legitimate voters from electoral rolls.Himachal Pradesh deputy chief minister Mukesh Agnihotri alleged that buses carrying supporters from his state were being stopped at different points on their way to Delhi.He claimed that some vehicles were intercepted over pollution norms and others over taxation issues, despite the buses being BS-VI-compliant.“We had already instructed everyone that such obstructions might occur, and if stopped, they should simply continue on foot to reach Himachal Bhawan,” Agnihotri said, adding that the supporters were prepared to walk to Ramlila Maidan.Himachal Pradesh minister Vikramaditya Singh called for accountability from Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and claimed that the number of votes involved in the alleged irregularities had risen from 13 crore to around 16 crore.“I am confident that, in the near future, the CEC Gyanesh Kumar will have to resign, and a new revolution will sweep across the entire country,” Singh said.Uttarakhand leader of opposition Yashpal Arya described the rally as a “battle for justice” to protect democracy and the Constitution. Congress leader Kunwar Danish Ali also called the mobilisation historic and accused the government of targeting students, young people and farmers.The INDIA bloc has demanded the replacement of electronic voting machines with paper ballots and the immediate resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner.Rahul Gandhi had appealed to people in Delhi and neighbouring states to join the march, either from Connaught Place or directly at Ramlila Maidan.Security has been tightened across the national capital in view of the two political events. Nearly 10,000 police and paramilitary personnel, including Delhi Police, Central Armed Police Forces, the CRPF and Rapid Action Force, have been deployed across Central and New Delhi, ANI reported.More than 4,000 personnel have been stationed around Ramlila Maidan, along the route from Minto Bridge and in surrounding areas. Barricades have also been placed around Connaught Place, Jantar Mantar, Bhagwan Das Road and areas near the Supreme Court and the Election Commission's office.Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita has been imposed in sensitive areas to prevent large unauthorised gatherings. Security agencies are also using CCTV cameras, AI-enabled facial recognition systems and drones to monitor crowd movement.At the Delhi-Gurugram border, Border Security Force personnel have been deployed alongside police units to monitor entry points into the capital. Authorities have installed barricades on major routes connecting the two cities and are checking suspicious vehicles.
Article Summary: Union minister JP Nadda launches sharp attack on the Congress and Rahul Gandhi over the INDIA bloc's rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan. He accuses the opposition of using the banner of democracy to create unrest, damage the economy and destabilise an elected government.

Article Title: 'No military solutions': EAM Jaishankar reveals PM Modi-Putin talks on Ukraine conflict in Delhi, Bishkek
Article Text:

India focuses on civilian shipping, grain exports and energy security

Jaishankar calls for diplomatic solutions to global conflicts

Jaishankar meets Russian, Polish and South Korean counterparts

NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar has said Prime Minister Narendra Modi discussed the Ukraine conflict with Russian President Vladimir Putin in New Delhi and earlier in Bishkek, as India continues diplomatic engagement with Moscow, Kyiv and Washington on measures to protect civilian shipping, restore grain exports and safeguard energy infrastructure.Speaking exclusively to news agency ANI on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Atlanta on Saturday, Jaishankar said India had held discussions with Russia, Ukraine and European countries on three key aspects of the conflict."Prime Minister himself had a discussion with President Putin in Delhi and before that in Bishkek," he said, referring to India's diplomatic engagement.Jaishankar said he had also discussed the conflict with Russian and Ukrainian officials, including during visits to Moscow and Kyiv, and in talks with Russian foreign minister Sergey Lavrov."We have also been coordinating this with the Americans because they have their own peace mediation initiative. So Secretary Rubio knows properly what is going on here," he said.Explaining the three areas under discussion, Jaishankar said India was first seeking to ensure that civilian vessels and seafarers were not targeted in the conflict.The second priority was to restore grain exports from Russia and Ukraine, both major suppliers to international markets.He said shipments through the Black Sea had fallen sharply because of the conflict."One not to attack civilian shipping and seafarers. The second is to find a way by which the grain exports from both Russia and Ukraine. Then these are two major exporters of grains for the global markets. Find a way of restoring that flow because that flow has cut down very sharply in the Black Sea," he said.The third area concerned energy infrastructure and shipments. Jaishankar said this was the most complicated issue because the concerns differed among the parties involved."Non-attack on energy is probably the most complicated piece because it means different things to the different players," he said, referring to refineries, electricity grids and ships carrying fuel.He added that India was trying to bring the parties together to address these concerns but could not publicly disclose the current status of the discussions.At the G20 meeting, the external affairs minister reiterated India's position that major international conflicts required diplomatic engagement rather than military escalation."Look, there are big conflicts today, two major conflicts which are having global ramifications," he said, adding that "there are no military solutions; we have to find a diplomatic pathway."Jaishankar also flagged the impact of disruptions in energy markets and fuel distribution on developing economies."This distortion of the energy markets, the politicisation of energy flows, this is something which is very harmful," he said, adding that the Global South was bearing the brunt of energy shortages.He also raised concerns over disruptions to grain shipments through the Black Sea and fertiliser shortages linked to tensions along the Persian Gulf and Red Sea corridors.On supply chain resilience, which was the focus of the G20 meeting's concluding plenary session, Jaishankar called for greater diversification of global production and manufacturing networks."Today we need more diversified supply chains," he said, advocating "more globalised, you know, more diversified production, more diversified manufacturing."In a post on X after the session, he said securing resilient supply chains was central to the well-being of the global economy. He also called for promoting the "right to industrialise", resisting "predatory practices" and pursuing the "de-politicisation of markets".On the sidelines of the G20 meeting, Jaishankar held separate discussions with his Russian, Polish and South Korean counterparts on the Ukraine conflict, West Asia, bilateral ties and multilateral issues.After meeting Lavrov, Jaishankar said the two sides had discussed the Ukraine conflict, the Gulf situation and multilateral issues.He also met Polish Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski, with discussions focusing on the Ukraine conflict, India-European Union ties and the G20."My meeting with DPM & FM Radosław Sikorski @sikorskiradek of Poland focused on the Ukraine conflict, India-EU ties and the G20," Jaishankar said.Poland is participating in this year's G20 meetings as a full participant following an invitation from the United States. It has also expressed interest in securing permanent membership of the grouping.Jaishankar separately met South Korean foreign minister Cho Hyun to review bilateral cooperation and discuss G20-related and other multilateral issues."Appreciated the stocktaking with @FMChoHyun of the Republic of Korea of our bilateral cooperation, as also the discussion on G20 and multilateral issues," he said.Earlier on Saturday, Jaishankar also participated in the Quad Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Atlanta with US secretary of state Marco Rubio, Japanese foreign minister Toshimitsu Motegi and Australian foreign minister Penny Wong.The US is holding the G20 presidency this year. After two days of discussions, Jaishankar and other foreign ministers attended a college football game between the Florida Gators and the Georgia Bulldogs at the Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta.
Article Summary: India continues diplomatic engagement with Moscow, Kyiv and Washington on measures to protect civilian shipping, restore grain exports and safeguard energy infrastructure. External affairs minister reiterated India's position that major international conflicts required diplomatic engagement rather than military escalation. Jaishankar held separate discussions with his Russian, Polish and South Korean counterparts on the Ukraine conflict.

Article Title: Fat-dissolving claims land FatX Solution in regulatory trouble; CDSCO cancels registration

NEW DELHI: Promising to dissolve fat cells may sound like an attractive pitch for a slimming product, but it has landed FatX Solution in trouble with the country's drug regulator. The Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) has cancelled the product's registration after finding that it was being promoted with claims that are not permitted for cosmetics.In an order dated October 28, CDSCO said Delhi-based importer Tekno Midas Aesthetics was marketing FatX Solution on its website as a product that could dissolve fat cells and reduce their size. The regulator said these were drug-related claims and did not fit the definition of a cosmetic under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940.The action followed a scrutiny of the company's application and website, during which CDSCO found differences between the claims being made online and those mentioned on the approved product label.Under the Cosmetics Rules, 2020, cosmetic products cannot make false or misleading claims. The rules define cosmetics as products meant for cleansing, beautifying, promoting attractiveness or altering appearance.Claims to dissolve fat cells go beyond this definition, the regulator said.CDSCO had issued a show-cause notice to the company on August 10, citing violations of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act and the Cosmetics Rules. The company submitted its response on September 1, but the regulator found it inconclusive and unsatisfactory. The firm also requested that its registration certificate be voluntarily surrendered.Rajan Bhatnagar of Tekno Midas Aesthetics told TOI that the product had been registered as a cosmetic more than four years ago. "At that time, the licence was granted because the product was registered as a cosmetic. The authorities have now changed their interpretation of the category under which the product falls. Earlier, it was considered a cosmetic, but now they say it falls under another category," he said.He said the company had decided not to contest the matter after receiving the notice. "We did not want to get into any dispute or challenge the notification. We voluntarily requested the surrender of the licence, and the authorities cancelled it," he said.The Central Licensing Authority subsequently cancelled the registration certificate, RC/COS-003300, which was issued in July 2022 and was valid until July 14, 2027. The cancellation took effect from October 28.
Article Summary: FatX Solution was marketed as a product that could dissolve fat cells and reduce their size. The product's registration has been cancelled by the country's drug regulator. CDSCO said the claims were drug-related and did not fit the definition of a cosmetic.

NEW DELHI: Central and state police forces personnel who put up a coordinated, decisive fight to eliminate armed Naxalism by March 31, 2026, figure prominently in the list of 490 Kendriya Grihmantri Dakshata Padak (Union home minister’s efficiency medal) awardees on Ekta Diwas this year.The two key ‘special operations’ in the Naxal theatre that fetched CRPF personnel 115 home minister’s medals include the second edition of Karreguttalu Hills (KGH-2) action undertaken in February this year and the ‘Operation Medhaburu’ in Jharkhand in January 2026. KGH-2 operation had played a decisive role in crushing the last bastion of CPI(Maoist) on the Chhattisgarh-Telangana border. It led to the surrender of top Naxal leaders Tippiri Thirupati alias Devuji and Malla Raji Reddy alias Sangram, and served as the last nail in the coffin for CPI(Maoist)’s top decision-making bodies, the politburo and central committee. As many as 19 CRPF personnel were honoured on Ekta Diwas, which commemorates the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, for success of the KGH-2 operation.As many as 96 CRPF personnel received the home minister’s medal for a key anti-Maoist operation undertaken in Saranda forests of Jharkhand. It nearly eliminated armed Naxalism in Jharkhand, having led to the killing of central committee member Patiram Manjhi alias Anal Da along with 14 others and forcing politburo member Misir Besra to run for cover; the latter was finally arrested from Dhanbad district in July 2026.The ‘Kendriya Grihmantri Daksha Padak’ — instituted in 2024 — recognises excellence in operations and investigation, exceptional performance, indomitable and daring intelligence service by personnel of the Central and state police forces, besides the meritorious work done by serving govt forensic scientists.While CRPF received the highest haul of home minister’s medals at 115 in the field of special operations, Chhattisgarh police personnel were honoured with 15 medals, Jharkhand police with 28, Telangana police with 21 and Maharashtra police with 7 medals.Other state/UT police honoured for operations include Delhi Police with 36 medals Punjab police with 37, Assam police (19) and Maharashtra police (7).In the investigation field, Central Board for Income-Tax and Customs (CBIC) walked away with 56 medals, CBI with 15, and National Investigation Agency (NIA) and Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) with five medals each. Among the state police honoured for excellence in investigation, are those of Maharashtra, NCT of Delhi, West Bengal, UP, Rajasthan, Bihar, Gujarat, Karnataka etc.In the forensic field, CFSL, Chandigarh was honoured with three medals, while the police in Bihar, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha and Tamil Nadu received a medal each.
Article Summary: 490 personnel across central and state forces are honoured on Ekta Diwas. CRPF personnel receive 115 Union home minister’s efficiency medals for anti-Naxal operations. Chhattisgarh police personnel were honoured with 15 medals, Jharkhand police with 28, Telangana police with 21 and Maharashtra police with 7 medals.

Article Title: CGHS cover for dependent widowed, divorced daughters after parents' death
Article Text: Widowed and divorced daughters returning to live with parents can now be added to their parents' Central Govt Health Scheme (CGHS) cards, even after the death of the govt employee or pensioner in whose name the original card was issued. Health ministry has allowed eligible daughters to be added or reinstated in cards held by family pensioners.The move will help parents supporting daughters with no independent income who need medical care. Earlier, once the original cardholder died and the spouse began receiving family pension, there was no provision to add or reinstate dependent family members.The ministry said it had received representations from pensioners facing difficulties supporting such daughters, particularly those with serious medical conditions requiring continued treatment. The benefit will not be automatic: authorities will verify daughter's marital status, income and dependency.All other CGHS eligibility conditions will continue to apply, the Oct 28 order said. It has been circulated to all central govt ministries and departments and DG of CGHS.
Article Summary: Widowed and divorced daughters returning to live with parents can now be added to their parents' Central Govt Health Scheme (CGHS) cards, even after the death of the govt employee or pensioner in whose name the original card was issued. The move will help parents supporting daughters with no independent income who need medical care.

Article Title: Sardar Patel had said if Pandit Nehru had not intervened, he would have integrated Kashmir as easily as Hyderabad: Rajnath Singh
Article Text:
Defence minister Rajnath Singh pays tribute to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel on his 151st birth anniversary, recalling his role in Hyderabad's integration and saying Patel could have integrated Kashmir as easily had Nehru not intervened.

NEW DELHI: Paying rich tributes to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel on his 151st birth anniversary, defence minister Rajnath Singh on Saturday recalled how the ‘Iron Man of India’ firmly dealt with the Nizam and Razakars, who sought to challenge India’s sovereignty and “laid the foundation of a strong and united India”. On the issue of Kashmir, Rajnath said, “Sardar Patel himself had said that if Pandit Nehru had not intervened, he would have integrated Kashmir as easily as Hyderabad.”Addressing a gathering, the defence minister said, “Sardar Patel was the architect of India’s political and territorial unity, whose extraordinary leadership, courage and unwavering commitment to national interest laid the foundation of a strong and united India”.He further said, “In democracy, govts are formed by winning the trust of the people and on the basis of public opinion, not through violence and anarchy. The path to change of power is elections, not coups. Those who challenge the unity and integrity of India should not forget the history of Sardar Patel.” “Those who dream of weakening India or creating disorder must remember that the land which gave birth to Sardar Patel has also given birth to Narendra Modi,” the minister said.He also criticised Congress and its allies for their use of the term 'regime change'. He emphasised that ‘regime change’ essentially implies a coup, violence, anarchy and civil war.Rajnath said that Sardar Patel firmly believed that India should never seek what does not belong to it, but should never give up what rightfully belongs to it, under any circumstances. He said that India continues to move forward guided by this very principle. “India does not seek to occupy anyone else's territory, nor does it initiate conflict. However, it remains resolute in securing what rightfully belongs to it and safeguarding its national interests. ”He further asserted that whether it is avenging terrorist attacks or reclaiming Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (POK), India remains firmly committed to defending its rights and sovereignty.Recalling the events surrounding the Congress presidential election of 1946, the minister said that despite overwhelming support from provincial Congress committees, Sardar Patel withdrew his candidature in deference to Mahatma Gandhi's wishes. “For Sardar Patel, the country was always bigger than the chair. Duty was more important than position, and national interest was greater than personal ambition. ”The defence minister expressed concern over what he described as the historical neglect of Sardar Patel’s contributions and recalled that Patel was conferred the Bharat Ratna only in 1991, nearly four decades after his demise. He also referred to the contrast between the celebrations of Jawaharlal Nehru's birth centenary in 1989 and the relatively subdued observance of Sardar Patel's birth centenary in 1975. He credited PM Modi with restoring national recognition to Patel's legacy through the Statue of Unity, Rashtriya Ekta Diwas, Run for Unity and Ekta March. “Sardar Patel was a great leader in his own right. Honouring him has not made him any greater; rather, it has brought greater honour to India.”Highlighting Sardar Patel's emphasis on military modernisation and indigenous production of weapons and ammunition, Rajnath said that India's growing defence manufacturing capabilities reflect the spirit of self-reliance that Patel advocated. He said that Sardar Patel's legacy extends far beyond the integration of princely states. It is reflected in India's strong administrative institutions, national security, social harmony and commitment to national interest. He said that the vision of 'Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat' and the mission of building a Viksit Bharat are inspired by the ideals that Sardar Patel upheld throughout his life.“India's greatest strength lies in its unity. We must never allow internal differences to weaken our national resolve. Preserving India's unity and integrity is the responsibility of every citizen,” he said.
Article Summary: Defence minister Rajnath Singh pays tribute to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel on his 151st birth anniversary. He recalled his role in Hyderabad's integration and said Patel could have integrated Kashmir as easily had Nehru not intervened. He also criticised Congress and its allies for their use of the term'regime change'

Article Title: PM lauds space scientists for successful launch of NVS-03; Isro chief says 2 more navigation sats to be launched to bolster constellation
Article Text:
PM Modi hailed Isro’s successful NVS-03 launch as a boost to NavIC, while the space agency plans two more navigation satellite launches in the coming months

NEW DELHI: With Isro successfully launching navigation satellite NVS-03, which carries an indigenously manufactured atomic clock, on Friday night from Sriharikota, PM Narendra Modi on Saturday called the GSLV-F18 mission “an important step in strengthening NavIC, our indigenous satellite navigation system”.Lauding Isro and its scientists, Modi said the “dedication and ingenuity of our space scientists continue to make our nation proud”. “Equipped with enhanced capabilities, NVS-03 will further our pursuit of self-reliance in critical technologies and support navigation services that benefit our people,” he further said on X on Saturday.Space minister Jitendra Singh said that “this remarkable achievement reflects India’s growing prowess in space technology and our unwavering commitment to strengthening sovereign indigenous navigation capabilities”.The success of the NVS-03 satellite mission will not only get India’s navigation system up and running again but also give a big boost to strategic forces as they have until now been dependent on foreign navigation systems like American GPS and Russian GLONASS for weapon and missile navigation.The advanced satellite has an indigenously developed atomic clock, which is the most accurate timekeeping device in the world.India has mastered this sophisticated technology and the desi atomic clock is now ticking in NVS-03 satellite in space.NavIC was until now not being used by the armed forces for the purposes of missile navigation, precise positioning and coordination of warships at sea, and indigenous navigation support for troop movement and combat aircraft. This is because four operational satellites were required for a standalone GPS-style position tracking system to work. The strategic forces were, therefore, dependent on foreign navigation systems. But the successful launch of NVS-03 has changed everything. It will make the NavIC constellation operational not only for strategic use but also for civilian purposes across India and up to 1,500 km (930 miles) beyond the country’s geographical borders.Indian security forces need an operational NavIC to maintain strategic autonomy and secure tactical advantage without relying on foreign-controlled networks. The four-satellite constellation will ensure secure, uncompromised communication, mobility and targeting data. Modern military hardware such as ballistic missiles and precision-guided munitions require highly accurate Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) signals to function effectively.Learning from past mistakes, Isro made an important change in the satellite system to make the launch successful. Isro chairman V Narayanan on Saturday revealed that in order to ensure mission reliability and bypass previous technical hurdles, the NVS-03 satellite was operated with “three pyro valves open”.Addressing the media at Sriharikota soon after the launch, Narayanan said that this bold technical decision was validated after rigorous vibration and shock testing by a national-level committee chaired by former Isro chief Kiran Kumar.Pyro valves are crucial in spacecraft propulsion. However, the NVS-02 satellite launched in 2025, the second spacecraft in the NVS series, was a failure due to a pryo valve-related problem. A high-level panel, after thorough analysis of the 2025 satellite failure, concluded that “the drive signal did not reach the pyro valve of the oxidiser line of the engine meant for orbit raising”.The Isro chief also informed that with four satellites, including NVS-01 now active in India's navigation satellite system, Isro plans to launch NVS-04 in five months, and NVS-05 in 10 months to further bolster the navigation satellite constellation.
Article Summary: PM Modi hails Isro’s successful NVS-03 launch as a boost to NavIC, while the space agency plans two more navigation satellite launches in the coming months. The advanced satellite has an indigenously developed atomic clock, which is the most accurate timekeeping device in the world.

Article Title: During Balen Shah's first India visit, Nepal to seek aid, investment
Article Text:
Nepal PM Balen Shah is expected to seek Indian aid for flood reconstruction, fresh hydropower investment and faster progress on stalled infrastructure projects during his proposed visit later this month

NEW DELHI: Nepal will seek Indian financial assistance for flood reconstruction, fresh investment in hydropower and faster implementation of stalled infrastructure projects during Prime Minister Balen Shah's proposed visit to India in late Nov. Indian foreign secretary Vikram Misri is expected in Kathmandu on Nov 4 to prepare the agenda for Shah's first bilateral foreign visit, which comes after months of diplomatic friction, including a postponed visit by Misri and differences over Lipulekh.Kathmandu wants the visit to produce concrete financial commitments, stronger energy cooperation and progress on projects that have remained pending despite earlier agreements. Both countries are also exploring infrastructure projects that could be inaugurated or launched during the visit.Shah's trip is expected in the latter half of Nov, although the dates have not been formally announced. New Indian ambassador Sudhakar Dalela is expected in Kathmandu on Nov 3, a day before Misri's proposed arrival. The foreign secretary is expected to hold discussions with senior Nepalese officials to finalise the agenda for the prime ministerial visit.
Article Summary: Nepal will seek Indian aid for flood reconstruction, fresh hydropower investment and faster progress on stalled infrastructure projects. Indian foreign secretary Vikram Misri is expected in Kathmandu on Nov 4 to prepare the agenda for Shah's first bilateral foreign visit.

Article Title: HC nixes NIA plea, upholds bail to J&K terror conspiracy accused
Article Text:
Delhi HC upholds bail granted to alleged J&K terror outfit overground worker, dismisses NIA’s appeal

NEW DELHI: Delhi high court has dismissed NIA's appeal against a trial court order granting bail to an alleged over ground worker in J&K, Mateen Ahmed Bhat, in a terror conspiracy case.A bench of Justices Navin Chawla and Arun Bhardwaj held that the trial court had passed the order after properly considering the restrictions on grant of bail under UAPA and examining whether the accusations against Bhat were prima facie true.The court further said neither was the bail order a final conclusion on the evidence nor did it discharge the accused. The subsequent framing of charges against Bhat was also deemed irrelevant by the bench while deciding NIA's appeal.The case relates to an alleged larger conspiracy involving the activities of proscribed terrorist organisations and the use of online platforms and local operatives to spread unrest in J&K.The high court observed that an appeal against the grant of bail has a limited scope and interference is warranted where the bail order is shown to be illegal, perverse, arbitrary or based on irrelevant considerations.
Article Summary: Delhi HC upholds bail granted to alleged J&K terror outfit overground worker, dismisses NIA’s appeal. NIA's appeal against a trial court order granting bail to Mateen Ahmed Bhat, in a terror conspiracy case.

Article Title: Darbar Move: J&K govt offices shift to Jammu
Article Text:
Jammu prepares to host government offices for the winter session as 91 departments shift from Srinagar under the 150-year-old Darbar Move tradition

JAMMU: The bi-annual Darbar Move of Jammu & Kashmir govt from Srinagar to Jammu began Saturday, with 91 offices scheduled to shift operations to the winter capital ahead of their reopening on Nov 2.“Offices closed in Srinagar today and will reopen in Jammu on Nov 2,” officials said.The annual tradition that dates back 150 years was stopped by L-G Manoj Sinha’s administration in June 2021, citing high financial costs and shift towards e-offices and paperless administration. CM Omar Abdullah restored it after taking office in 2024, as had been promised in National Conference’s election manifesto, and the practice resumed in Nov 2025.Ahead of offices reopening, Jammu is undergoing its customary makeover, with traffic department installing new road dividers and regulating vehicular movement.In view of convoy movement, authorities restricted heavy and medium motor vehicles carrying goods on NH-44 on Saturday-Sunday. The advisory asked transporters carrying fresh and perishable goods and livestock to plan their movement accordingly.
Article Summary: The bi-annual Darbar Move of Jammu & Kashmir govt from Srinagar to Jammu began Saturday. 91 offices scheduled to shift operations to the winter capital ahead of their reopening on Nov 2. The annual tradition that dates back 150 years was stopped by L-G Manoj Sinha’s administration in June 2021.
